steps.where: Admin › Administration (Accounts), top bar › Create workspace, then Project access
steps.do: Create the second person, a workspace for the lab, and put them in it. On Administration enter reviewer as User ID and reviewer-pass-123 as Password and click Create account. Click the + next to the workspace selector in the top bar, name the workspace, and click Create and select. Back on Administration, choose the workspace under Project for access management, enter the reviewer's user id, pick the Reviewer role and click Add member. (The reviewer's platform scopes come from the environment variables in the README's setup section.)
steps.click: Create account, Create and select, then Add member
steps.see: The top bar shows the new workspace as active, and the Project members table lists reviewer with the role reviewer.
steps.asset: account: reviewer, workspace: invoice-intake, member: reviewer

steps.where: Agent resources › Object Store › Bucket browser
steps.do: Create the two buckets the pipeline reads from and writes to. Type the bucket name into the new-bucket-name field and click + (Create bucket). Do it twice.
steps.see: Both buckets appear in the Bucket browser next to caliber-workspaces, the bucket the server keeps for itself.

steps.do: Open doc-intake, click New folder, name it incoming and click Create. Open the folder and click Upload; select all 30 files from the sources folder at once. The upload keeps each file name, so the keys become incoming/<file name>.
steps.see: The folder lists 30 objects, from empty.txt (0 B) to inv-2026-0123-oversized.txt (about 120 KB).

steps.where: Agent resources › Object Store › doc-intake › incoming
steps.do: Check the pipeline will see what you think it will. Click the View preview (eye) action on inv-2026-0101-acme.txt.
steps.see: The preview dialog shows the invoice text, starting Acme Industrial Supply Co. and containing Invoice No: INV-2026-0101. This is the text the workflow's Input Bucket node will read.

steps.do: Install the pipeline. On Document-to-JSON Pipeline click Install, give the workflow a name, tick the prerequisites acknowledgement and click Install paused draft. The Studio opens on the draft with every node on the canvas.
steps.see: The editor outline lists read_document, extract_fields, validate_schema, package_result, route, emit_extracted, write_extracted, review_gate, emit_reviewed, write_reviewed and final. Validate answers Valid.

steps.do: The cookbook installs paused. Open the workflow's page and click Resume, then open the editor again and click Run monitor.
steps.see: The button now reads Pause, and the run monitor opens without the This workflow is paused note.

steps.where: Agent resources › Workflows › doc-intake-to-json › Run monitor
steps.do: Run a valid invoice. Type the object key into the run input and click Run. Then run the yen invoice; it is valid under this version too.
steps.see: The status badge reaches Completed within a few seconds and the Execution Debugger's step map lists write_extracted. The yen invoice also completes and its JSON is written.

steps.where: Agent resources › Workflows › doc-intake-to-json › Run monitor
steps.do: Run the same invoice sent again under another file name.
steps.see: The run ends Failed and the monitor shows output_bucket write failed for 'invoices/INV-2026-0101.json': object already exists. The first invoice's JSON is not touched.

steps.where: Agent resources › Workflows › doc-intake-to-json › Run monitor
steps.do: Run an invoice whose total is missing, then try to approve your own run, then start a second invalid invoice (no vendor) that you will reject.
steps.see: The badge reads Awaiting approval at review_gate. Clicking Approve as the account that started the run shows the account that triggered this run cannot approve it; a second person must decide and the run stays awaiting approval.

steps.where: Top bar › Log out, then sign in as reviewer
steps.do: Sign in as reviewer, select the workspace, open the workflow editor and the run monitor, select the first held run, click Approve, then Resume. Select the second held run and click Reject.
steps.see: The first run ends Completed and the step map lists write_reviewed. The second ends Failed.
steps.asset: runs: one approved and completed, one rejected

steps.do: Check what reached the output bucket. Open invoices and preview INV-2026-0101.json; open reviewed.
steps.see: The preview contains "invoice_number": "INV-2026-0101" and "total": 646.92. The reviewed folder holds inv-2026-0115-no-total.json and nothing for the rejected document.

steps.do: Version 1 is final. Sign in as admin again, select the workspace, open the workflow's editor and click Publish: run validation, tick the acknowledgement if shown, Next, Next, Publish.
steps.see: The message reads Published., the header changes from v1 · draft to v1 · published and a banner says the version is read-only.

steps.do: Finance wants yen invoices checked by a person. Click Restore as draft in the banner, select the validate_schema node, delete "JPY" from the currency list in its config, click Save, then publish as before.
steps.see: The editor opens v2 · draft, shows Saved, and after publishing reads v2 · published.
steps.asset: workflow version v2 published (JPY removed from the schema's currency list)

steps.where: Agent resources › Workflows › doc-intake-to-json › Run monitor
steps.do: Re-run the yen invoice on version 2.
steps.see: The badge reads Awaiting approval at review_gate: the same document that completed under version 1 is now held, and nothing new is written.

steps.do: Compare the versions. Open the workflow's page, the Versions tab, and pick v1 · published as the base and v2 · published to compare. Then open the Runs tab.
steps.see: The diff lists validate_schema as the modified node. The Runs tab shows the two yen runs: one Completed (v1), one Awaiting approval (v2).
